site_meta_description: Desktop app for Claude Code, Codex, Muse Code and opencode, one worktree per thread.
site_pricing_meta_description: HinaCode is free and open source, with every feature included.
site_hero_lede: Coding agent orchestration for Claude Code, Codex, Muse Code, opencode, or magpie.
site_hero_shot_alt: A thread waiting for approval, thread list beside it
site_loop_review_1_body: See the last turn's change or the whole worktree, and comment on a line.
site_loop_review_2_body: Changed files grouped by intent, with notes on the tricky parts.
site_loop_review_3_body: Open the dev server beside the transcript, and click an element to add it to your message.
site_loop_review_4_body: A shell per worktree, an editor for small fixes, and the ports agents leave open.
site_review_shot_alt: The Files panel marking lines an agent changed
site_tools_vm_body: A throwaway Linux desktop per thread. The agent drives it, and you take over to sign in. Runs on boat.dev with an API key, or bring your own VM on your sbx host.
site_tools_secret: Ask you for an API key. It lands in a file, not the transcript.
site_tools_threads: Give a side task to a new thread, or ask another agent to weigh in.
site_tools_watch: Wake the agent when its pull request needs it.
site_tools_read: Read another thread's work, here or on another machine.
site_tools_devices: iOS simulators and Android emulators for mobile checks.
site_tools_linear: Read Linear issues and post the pull request back.
site_remote_machines_body: Run npx hinacode serve on a Mac mini or a cloud box. Its projects join your sidebar, and each thread shows where it runs.
site_remote_relay_body: Sign in to link a machine to your account. The relay reaches it from your phone, laptop or code.hinacode.app.
site_remote_phone_body: iPhone, iPad and Android. See who needs you, then approve, answer, steer and merge.
site_remote_private_body: Connections listen only on the address you pick, such as Tailscale. Each device holds its own credential.
site_remote_phone_alt: HinaCode phone app showing an approval card
site_agents_lede: HinaCode runs the claude, codex, muse and opencode CLIs you are signed in to. No markup, nothing between you and the provider.
site_agents_magpie_title: A unified experience for managing all your AI agents.
site_agents_magpie: Or pick magpie, and a thread runs any model your gateway serves: DeepSeek, Kimi, OpenRouter, or a ChatGPT or Claude plan.
site_faq_cost_a: Nothing. Every feature is free and MIT licensed.
site_faq_agents_a: Claude Code, Codex, Muse Code and opencode, plus any model behind a magpie gateway. Install and sign in to each CLI you want.
site_faq_code_q: Does my code leave my machine?
site_faq_code_a: Only where the agent CLIs already send it. HinaCode runs locally, with data in a SQLite file.
site_faq_stable_q: Is it ready for daily use?
site_faq_stable_a: It is in alpha, built daily with HinaCode, shipping several times a day. Expect bugs, and report them on GitHub.
site_faq_platforms_a: macOS on Apple silicon, Windows, and Linux as an AppImage. The server runs on Node 24.
site_cta_lede: Free and open source. Bring your own agent CLIs.
site_footer_tagline: A desktop app for running coding agents in parallel.
site_footer_license: Open source under the MIT license.
site_pricing_lede: No seats, no tiers and no trial. HinaCode is open source under the MIT license.
site_pricing_item_2: Claude Code, Codex, Muse Code and opencode
site_pricing_item_4: Approvals, questions, steering and queued messages
site_pricing_item_5: Diffs, line comments and the pull request guide
site_pricing_item_7: Routines on a schedule or a webhook
site_pricing_item_8: Remote machines and the phone app
site_pricing_costs_body: Your agent plans. HinaCode runs the Claude Code, Codex, Muse Code and opencode CLIs you're signed in to, so usage counts against those plans or API keys, the same as in a terminal.
mobile_pairing_lead: On the desktop, open Settings, Connections, and turn on Allow remote control. Scan the QR code it shows, or paste the pairing URL. A cloud prints its QR code when you run hinacode serve, or hinacode pair later.
mobile_pairing_invalid: This is not a HinaCode pairing URL. Copy it again from Settings, Connections on the desktop, or run hinacode pair on a cloud.
mobile_pairing_camera_needed: HinaCode needs the camera to read the pairing QR code.
mobile_composer_fast_mode_hint: Faster responses that use more of your plan
mobile_artifact_doc_description: Write a design doc, report, review or plan
mobile_artifact_writing_description: Write a blog post, release notes or an announcement
mobile_artifacts_empty_hint: Pages, documents and whiteboards your agents publish show up here.
mobile_document_conflict: The agent changed this document while you were editing.
mobile_document_read_only: The phone cannot edit this document without changing it, so it opens read-only.
mobile_workspace_project_root_hint: Switches the project root to this branch
mobile_workspace_new_worktree_hint: Its own checkout, on a new branch from this one
mobile_terminal_control_hint: Applies Control to the next key you type
mobile_terminal_gone: The desktop no longer has this shell.
mobile_transport_not_sent: Not sent. The desktop was unreachable for a minute.
mobile_transport_may_have_run: The desktop was unreachable for a minute. The action may still have run.
mobile_transport_lost_reply: The connection dropped before the desktop answered. The action may still have run.
mobile_transport_token_rotated: The server's token was rotated. Pair again with the new QR code.
mobile_transport_token_refused: The server refused this token. Pair again from Settings, Connections on the desktop, or with hinacode pair on a cloud.
mobile_transport_protocol_mismatch: The desktop speaks remote protocol {desktop}, this app speaks {app}. Update the older one.
mobile_connection_server_gone: No paired server has this anymore.
pr_open_in_window: Open changes in a new window
web_vm_screen_desktop_only: The Tiny VM screen opens only in the desktop app.
web_signed_out: This browser was signed out. Sign in again.
web_machine_refused_token: {name} refused its token. Reload this page after it publishes a new one to the relay.
web_relay_unreachable: Could not reach the relay. Check the address and your connection.
web_relay_bad_answer: The relay sent an answer this page cannot read.
web_no_machines: The relay shows no machines yet. Turn on the relay on a machine, then reload this page.
web_transport_not_sent: Not sent. The machine was unreachable for a minute.
web_transport_may_have_run: The machine was unreachable for a minute. The action may still have run.
web_transport_lost_reply: The connection dropped before the machine answered. The action may still have run.
web_transport_token_rotated: The machine's token was rotated. Reload this page to pick up the new one from the relay.
web_transport_token_refused: The machine refused its token. Reload this page after it publishes a new one to the relay.
web_transport_protocol_mismatch: The machine speaks remote protocol {machine}, this page speaks {app}. Update the older one.
web_notifications_denied_hint: Allow notifications for this site in your browser's site settings. Browsers only allow them on HTTPS pages.
web_notifications_not_determined_hint: Your browser asks once you click Allow notifications.
site_artifacts_lede: Agents publish their work beside the thread. You answer on the page, not in the chat.
site_artifacts_document_body: Reports and plans you can edit. Select a line to comment, and the agent replies on it.
site_artifacts_document_alt: A startup audit document with an agent's question on one line
site_artifacts_whiteboard_body: The agent sketches the design. Draw on it, select a part and press Ask.
site_artifacts_whiteboard_alt: A whiteboard of the relay that an agent drew
site_remote_lede: Agents run where the code lives. You drive them from the desktop, a browser or your phone.
site_remote_shot_alt: A thread running on a Mac mini, waiting for approval in the desktop app
